note: Machine-readable mirror of the reversibility gates in docs/requirements.md §10. Governance metadata about this repository, not COLREGS data — it deliberately lives in docs/ rather than data/, which is the consumer-facing model. REQ-GATE-3 is enforced against this file by test/data.test.mjs; the prose section is authoritative for the reasoning, this file is authoritative for status.

closing_events.1.0-tag: the 1.0 version tag — REQ-GATE-3 blocks it until every gate carrying this closing event has been re-taken
closing_events.first-non-english-corpus: the second corpus of any one jurisdiction, which in practice is the first non-English text
closing_events.first-community-translation-of-national-: the first `community`-tier translation of a `national`-tier corpus
closing_events.first-external-contribution: the first merged contribution from someone other than the copyright holder
closing_events.none: the decline does not get cheaper or dearer with time; recorded so it is not re-read as merely deferred

statuses.open: declined for now, not re-taken; adoption still possible at the stated cost
statuses.re-taken: reconsidered deliberately and confirmed as declined, in the cited ADR
statuses.adopted: the declined design was subsequently adopted, in the cited ADR
statuses.declined-permanently: declined on grounds that do not decay; no closing event exists

gates.title: `paragraph_id` split from `citation_path`
gates.trigger: a paragraph path that keeps its spelling while changing what text it denotes — an upstream renumbering, or (the near-term case, Q-8) a national amalgamation whose paragraph structure diverges from `intl` below rule level
gates.note: Open on timing, not outcome: if the trigger fires the split is forced and lands as a major version. Also re-checked before the second jurisdiction, whichever comes first.

gates.title: instrument → edition → corpus as first-class layers
gates.trigger: a jurisdiction publishing two editions in force concurrently

gates.title: legal-status × translation-status as two enums
gates.trigger: a real corpus whose legal tier and translation tier disagree in a way a consumer must filter on and cannot from the metadata as structured
gates.note: Half-adopted: one tier for legal authority (REQ-LANG-3), translation provenance as structured metadata (REQ-LANG-8, REQ-PROV-6).

gates.title: a package-encoded language fallback chain
gates.note: The door opens outward: loosening REQ-LANG-7 later is additive, tightening it later would break consumers. Recorded so the asymmetry is not re-discovered as an argument for adopting early.

gates.title: a CI-enforced terminology glossary
gates.note: Declined for legal corpora — it follows from verbatimness (REQ-MODEL-1) and does not decay. For display catalogs it is contributor guidance, gated on contribution docs existing at all.

gates.title: the compilation's outbound licence
gates.trigger: deciding the data side wants CC0 or CC BY 4.0 separately from the code (REQ-PROV-4, Q-9)
gates.note: ADR 0004 settles the code licence (MIT → Apache-2.0) and leaves the data licence open. Already-published npm versions stay under the licence they shipped with; the gate governs future releases only, and may be held open deliberately with a DCO or CLA.
